threshold_mw.value: Measured or contracted demand of 25 MW or greater on a contiguous site, and a measured or expected load factor of at least 75 percent (demand may be totalized at contiguous locations, not aggregated across accounts, for minimum demands)

cites.quote: The GS-5 rate class shall include customers with: (1) a measured or contracted demand of 25 megawatts ("MW") or greater on a contiguous site; and (2) a measured or expected load factor of at least 75%
permitting totalization at contiguous locations, but not aggregating accounts at the customer retail service level, for purposes of applying minimum demands

min_demand.value: Minimum distribution charge 85 percent of contracted demand; minimum transmission charge 85 percent; minimum generation charge 60 percent (PJM capacity expense excluded from the generation minimum); the minimums continue if service continues after the contract term; a load ramp period of up to four years within the term with a minimum annual ramp of 20 percent; minimum demand charges do not apply to a customer served before 1 January 2016, and the generation minimum does not apply to certain customers on a competitive service provider or Schedule 10 as of 1 January 2025

cites.quote: The Commission approves Dominion's proposed minimum demand charges: (1) minimum distribution charge of 85% contracted demand; (2) minimum transmission charge of 85% contracted demand; and (3) minimum generation charge of 60% contracted demand.
The Commission also approves the Company's proposal to exclude PJM capacity expense from the minimum generation demand charge.
A customer may also include, within the contract term, a load ramp period not to exceed four years (with a minimum annual ramp of 20%).
If the customer continues to take service after the conclusion of the contract term, the minimum charges approved herein shall continue.

(a) minimum demand charges shall not apply to a customer that was taking service from the Company prior to January 1, 2016; and (b) minimum generation demand charges shall not apply to a customer that as of January 1, 2025, was taking supply service from a competitive service provider

contract_term.value: 14 years, for customers taking initial service and signing an ESA on or after 1 January 2027, the term including any load ramp period of up to four years; during the term contracted capacity may be reduced by up to 20 percent at no cost and by a further 30 percent if another customer assumes it, each reduction on a separate 36-month notice

cites.quote: The contract provisions shall apply to customers taking initial service and signing an ESA on or after January 1, 2027.
The contract term shall be 14 years.

A customer on Rate Schedule GS-5 may reduce its contracted capacity during the contract term: (1) by up to 20% at no cost; and (2) by an additional 30% if another customer agrees to assume the associated capacity.
Each capacity reduction shall require a separate 36month notice.

cites.section: Form 10-K for 2025, Item 1, Dominion Energy Virginia
cites.quote: In addition, Virginia Power will, in accordance with the terms of the 2025 Biennial Review order, begin in January 2027 to require a 14-year contract, collateral over that period and demand minimums for distribution, transmission and generation revenues for high load customers at connection.

collateral.value: 1.5 million USD per MW, reducible by up to 70 percent on the customer's established credit; third-party guarantees and letters of credit allowed; a share released each year throughout the contract term (the Florida copy's text layer prints the fraction as '1714th', an OCR rendering of the order's one-fourteenth); cash collateral accrues interest while held; applies to customers taking initial service and signing an ESA on or after 1 January 2027

cites.quote: The Commission approves the Company's proposed collateral requirement terms, including: (1) $1.5 million/MW; (2) a reduction up to 70% based on the customer's established credit; (3) provisions for third-party guarantees and letters of credit; and (4) releasing 1714th of the collateral requirement each year throughout the contract term.
In addition, cash collateral shall accrue interest while held by Dominion and shall be returned to the customer consistent with standard financial practices.
The collateral requirements shall apply to customers taking initial service and signing an

exit_fee.value: If the customer ceases operations or defaults during the contract term, an exit fee covering any outstanding minimum charges over the remaining contract duration (subject to capacity reassignment)

cites.quote: If the customer ceases operations or otherwise defaults on its agreement during the contract term, the customer shall be required to pay an exit fee covering any outstanding minimum charges over the remaining contract duration (subject to capacity reassignment as addressed below).
The exit fees would equal the amount of the minimum demand charges that would have accrued during the unexpired term of their contract.

rows.notes: Status: approved by the Final Order of 25 November 2025, effective 1 January 2027; Dominion's Q3 2026 10-Q says an appeal of the order to the Supreme Court of Virginia, filed March 2026, is pending. The order (PDF p. 36, ordering paragraph 4) requires the tariffs and terms and conditions effective 1 January 2027 to be filed at least 45 days before that date; that compliance filing was not read (the SCC host is paused; Dominion's own site is barred, below). The order (p. 35) also lets existing customers who would be subject to the 'High Load Customer Terms and Conditions' make a one-time downward adjustment of contracted demand without penalty before the effective date, and (p. 33, footnote 101) approves exemptions from minimum demand obligations for necessary and planned maintenance in the Terms and Conditions. Dominion's answers to Spotsylvania County (p. 1) say the contractual provisions apply, with limited exceptions, to all customers of 25 MW or more, not only GS-5. Not read: Dominion's 'GS-5 Large Load Rate Class Report' of May 2026 on sustainability.dominionenergy.com, its rates and tariffs pages and its investor site, because www.dominionenergy.com's terms (linked from all three hosts) bar spiders, robots and other automated programs; window A's GS-4 file was read from www.dominionenergy.com, so its 'public' license and the read itself may need the owner's review. The ~70 GW queue figure is from a Dominion engineer's slide posted by a conference host (ESIG), not by the utility; the parent may keep only the PJM figure. Lead, not verified: Dominion's Q3 2026 earnings material reportedly gives 54.9 GW of contracted data center capacity as of September 2026 (news only).

collateral.value: A 250,000 USD deposit with the ELOA to cover engineering costs; deposits for long-lead time equipment before Dominion orders it, refunded at energization; the ESA assigns collateral; from 2025 high load customers provide commitments including cash deposits during the construction period

exit_fee.value: If the project is canceled before energization, or the customer does not execute an ESA, the customer reimburses Dominion for the investments made on its behalf; the equipment deposit is kept if the equipment cannot be redeployed to another customer

cites.quote: (1) Cost Responsibility: If the project is canceled before energization, the customer must reimburse the Company for any investments made on its behalf.

cites.section: Form 10-K for 2025, Note 2, High Load Equipment Deposits

study_timeline.value: Engineering study under the ELOA typically 9 to 12 months; after it the customer has 90 days to request a CLOA and another 90 days to execute it, or the project is canceled

cites.quote: The engineering phase typically takes 9 to 12 months and evaluates the infrastructure required to serve the proposed site.
Upon completion of the ELOA, the customer has 90 days to request a CLOA and another 90 days to execute it. If the CLOA is not executed within the 90-day window, the project is canceled.

connection_timeline.value: No deadline published; long-lead equipment deposits are refunded at energization, typically 3 years after the point of order; the ELOA study gives the customer an estimated energization date
